title: Is My Phone Still Getting Updates?
youtube_title: Is Your Phone Too Old for Security Updates? How to Check | Fix It Friday
next: Next Friday: My Phone Battery Dies Too Fast
description: Phones don't get security updates forever. Kip and Bub show how to check for updates on an iPhone or Android phone, how to find your phone's security date, and what to do if your phone has stopped getting updates.
tags: is my phone still getting updates

scenes.say: Is your phone still getting security updates? Most people never check. And this month, some popular phones, like Google's Pixel 6, reach the end of their update window.
It's Fix It Friday. Today: is my phone still getting updates?
Security updates are fixes that patch holes criminals use to break in. Phone makers only send them for a few years. After that, the phone still works, but those holes stay open.
On an iPhone, open Settings, then General, then Software Update. If an update is waiting, tap Update Now.
On an Android phone, open Settings and look for Software update, or System, then Software updates. The names change a little between brands.

Here's a handy trick for Android. In Settings, open About phone and look for the security update date, sometimes called security patch level. If it's many months old and no update shows up, your phone may be out of support.
If your phone has stopped getting updates, don't panic. It won't stop working tomorrow. But start planning for a newer phone, and be extra careful with links in texts and emails until then.
When you shop, ask how many years of updates the phone gets. Many newer phones promise five years or more. That's money well spent.

card.text: Ask: how many years of updates?

scenes.say: And watch out. A pop-up or text saying your phone is infected or out of date, with a link or a number to call, is a scam. Real updates only come from your phone's Settings.
So: check Settings for updates, look at your security date, plan ahead if your phone is out of support, and ignore scary pop-ups.
